messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'us-west-2/gpupool-1' at 98% allocation. Autoscaler failed to add new instances (reason: scale_limit_reached). Queue length spike -> 4.2k pending requests. Paging oncall: @sam :rotating_light:

sam: Oncall here. seeing 429s from the frontend and high queue depth. pulling graphs now.

maya: I can see the autoscaler logs: 
```
scale_request: +120 GPUs
reason: queue_threshold
result: rejected (policy=max_pool_capacity)
```
There was a recent config change that lowered max_pool_capacity by 20% yesterday (PR #3123).

leo: On top of that, scheduler reports heavy fragmentation: lots of GPUs carved as MIG 1g slices while the main large-model pool needs 8g equivalents. Those 1g slices are unused for our LLM routing -> effectively stranded capacity.

ines: Customers: support dashboard shows a burst of errors for accounts: acct-A, acct-B, acct-C — high priority customers hitting timeouts. I've opened support tickets and notified CS.

sam: Thanks. Immediate plan: 1) stop accepting new long-running generation jobs (apply temporary request filter). 2) Route small-embedding/fast calls to a fallback cluster. 3) Try to increase pool limit if cloud quota allows.

maya: I'm going to attempt an emergency canary to increase max_pool_capacity to allow 120 additional GPU slots. if cloud quota is the blocker, we need ops-runner to request emergency quota bump.

ops-runner: Requesting quota bump now with cloud support, ETA unknown but I'll mark as high priority. Meanwhile we can do local mitigation.

leo: Local mitigation: we can rebalance MIG slices on a subset of nodes to aggregate freed 1g slices into contiguous capacity for 8g placements. That will require node reboots or stopping some low-priority jobs. Time estimate ~7-12 minutes for a targeted pool of 6 nodes.

sam: Can we do a partial rebalance only on burnout nodes to free 2x8g equivalents? we need to avoid wholesale disruption.

leo: Yes — plan: pick nodes n-12..n-17 (low-util), cordon + drain non-critical pods, run mig-merge script, uncordon. I'll post the command.

leo: ```bash
# target nodes
for n in n-12 n-13 n-14 n-15 n-16 n-17; do
  kubectl cordon $n
  kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  ssh root@$n 'sudo /opt/mig-tools/mig-merge --profile=8g --force'
  kubectl uncordon $n
done
```

maya: Note: draining will evict some lightweight inference jobs. We'll redirect those to the fallback pool. I've pre-warmed fallback hosts with smaller models.

ines: I've told acct-A/B/C about degraded performance and that we're actively mitigating; gave ETA 30-60m. No data loss.

sam: Good. Also enable early-fail for long requests so they don't clog the queue. Switch config: `request.max_runtime_ms=60000` for new requests.

deploy-bot: deploy: patch applied to route-filter v2 (hash: d2f9c4). Rolling update started -> 4/8 nodes updated.

ops-runner: Cloud support responded: no immediate quota bump, but suggested temp-resize by spinning up preemptible instances in us-west-2. Asking permission to launch 40 preemptible GPUs.

maya: Approve preemptible add. Launch them with lower-priority routing and short TTL so they don't stay after the surge.

sam: Approving. Make sure we tag and metric them separately. Also add fallback to not schedule heavy 8g workloads there unless after mig-merge.

leo: mig-merge started on n-12..n-17. progress: nodes n-12,n-13 completed; n-14 in progress. So far freed 2x8g equivalents.

ops-runner: Preemptible instances launching: 40 GPUs requested -> 32 available immediately, 8 queued. We'll route embeddings and low-cost routes there.

sam: Monitoring queues and 429s. queue depth dropping from 4200 -> 1100 over last 10 minutes. 429 rate reduced to 12% -> 3% over 15m.

ines: Customer update: acct-A reports partial recovery, still some timeouts but improved. acct-B upgraded plan temporarily; they accepted mitigation note.

leo: mig-merge completed on the targeted nodes. Executing controlled scheduler rebalance to place large jobs onto the newly coalesced 8g slices. Running placement command: `scheduler rebalance --policy=prefer-new-slices --threshold=0.5`

maya: Rebalance in progress. CPU/IO and network metrics look normal. No pod restarts beyond the expected drained ones.

sam: Deploy-bot reports route-filter rolled out fully. Also enabled early-fail. Keep throttles for low-priority traffic.

ops-runner: Cloud preemptibles are up and accepting traffic for small models. No billing alerts yet.

support-bot: Open incidents/tickets updated: INC-9021 (acct-A), INC-9022 (acct-B), INC-9023 (acct-C). Noted mitigation steps and ETA next update in 30m.

sam: Current status: partial mitigation successful. Queue now 180 pending, 429s ~1.1%. Primary risk: fragmentation remains in other pools. Need follow-ups: 1) revert yesterday's max_pool_capacity reduction or justify it (maya). 2) audit MIG sizing policy (leo). 3) add autoscaler fallback to allow temporary oversubscribe/burstpool when queue spike and quota unavailable (sam/maya). 4) customer postmortem and timeline (ines/support).

maya: I'll open an emergency PR to restore previous max limits and add a feature flag to gate it. PR #3178 -> requesting expedited review from infra-team.

leo: I'll draft a runbook change: add routine defragmentation and a heuristics-based mig-merge during low-traffic windows. Also propose the scheduler accept fractional placements when possible.

ines: Drafting customer-facing postmortem to send within 4 hours, will include scope, impact, and mitigations.

sam: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the live incident log. If anyone notices regression or cloud quota updates, drop it here. I'll escalate to incident commander if scope widens.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded from SEV2 -> SEV3.

sam: Closing live mitigation phase. Follow-ups created: TASK-453 (restore pool limit), TASK-454 (autoscaler fallback), TASK-455 (defrag runbook), TASK-456 (customer pmo). We'll reconvene after postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
